import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

class HomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β] where
  map_top : ∀ (f : F), f ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot : ∀ (f : F), f ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg : ∀ (f : F) (φ : α), f (∼ φ) = ∼f φ
  map_imply : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ➝ ψ) = f φ ➝ f ψ
  map_and : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋏ ψ) = f φ ⋏ f ψ
  map_or  : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋎ ψ) = f φ ⋎ f ψ

attribute [simp] HomClass.map_top HomClass.map_bot HomClass.map_neg HomClass.map_imply HomClass.map_and HomClass.map_or

namespace HomClass

variable (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β]
variable [HomClass F α β]
variable (f : F) (a b : α)

instance : CoeFun F (fun _ => α → β) := ⟨DFunLike.coe⟩

@[simp] lemma map_iff : f (a ⭤ b) = f a ⭤ f b := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff]

end HomClass

variable (α β γ : Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [LogicalConnective γ]

structure Hom where
  toTr : α → β
  map_top' : toTr ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot' : toTr ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg' : ∀ φ, toTr (∼φ) = ∼toTr φ
  map_imply' : ∀ φ ψ, toTr (φ ➝ ψ) = toTr φ ➝ toTr ψ
  map_and' : ∀ φ ψ, toTr (φ ⋏ ψ) = toTr φ ⋏ toTr ψ
  map_or'  : ∀ φ ψ, toTr (φ ⋎ ψ) = toTr φ ⋎ toTr ψ

infix:25 " →ˡᶜ " => Hom
annotation: infix:25 " →ˡᶜ " => Hom

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

class HomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β] where
  map_top : ∀ (f : F), f ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot : ∀ (f : F), f ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg : ∀ (f : F) (φ : α), f (∼ φ) = ∼f φ
  map_imply : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ➝ ψ) = f φ ➝ f ψ
  map_and : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋏ ψ) = f φ ⋏ f ψ
  map_or  : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋎ ψ) = f φ ⋎ f ψ

attribute [simp] HomClass.map_top HomClass.map_bot HomClass.map_neg HomClass.map_imply HomClass.map_and HomClass.map_or

namespace HomClass

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

class HomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β] where
  map_top : ∀ (f : F), f ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot : ∀ (f : F), f ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg : ∀ (f : F) (φ : α), f (∼ φ) = ∼f φ
  map_imply : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ➝ ψ) = f φ ➝ f ψ
  map_and : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋏ ψ) = f φ ⋏ f ψ
  map_or  : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋎ ψ) = f φ ⋎ f ψ

attribute [simp] HomClass.map_top HomClass.map_bot HomClass.map_neg HomClass.map_imply HomClass.map_and HomClass.map_or

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

class HomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β] where
  map_top : ∀ (f : F), f ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot : ∀ (f : F), f ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg : ∀ (f : F) (φ : α), f (∼ φ) = ∼f φ
  map_imply : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ➝ ψ) = f φ ➝ f ψ
  map_and : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋏ ψ) = f φ ⋏ f ψ
  map_or  : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋎ ψ) = f φ ⋎ f ψ

attribute [simp] HomClass.map_top HomClass.map_bot HomClass.map_neg HomClass.map_imply HomClass.map_and HomClass.map_or

namespace HomClass

variable (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β]
variable [HomClass F α β]
variable (f : F) (a b : α)

instance : CoeFun F (fun _ => α → β) := ⟨DFunLike.coe⟩

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

class HomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β] where
  map_top : ∀ (f : F), f ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot : ∀ (f : F), f ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg : ∀ (f : F) (φ : α), f (∼ φ) = ∼f φ
  map_imply : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ➝ ψ) = f φ ➝ f ψ
  map_and : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋏ ψ) = f φ ⋏ f ψ
  map_or  : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋎ ψ) = f φ ⋎ f ψ

attribute [simp] HomClass.map_top HomClass.map_bot HomClass.map_neg HomClass.map_imply HomClass.map_and HomClass.map_or

namespace HomClass

variable (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β]
variable [HomClass F α β]
variable (f : F) (a b : α)

instance : CoeFun F (fun _ => α → β) := ⟨DFunLike.coe⟩

@[simp] lemma map_iff : f (a ⭤ b) = f a ⭤ f b := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff]

end HomClass

variable (α β γ : Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [LogicalConnective γ]

structure Hom where
  toTr : α → β
  map_top' : toTr ⊤ = ⊤

  map_neg' : ∀ φ, toTr (∼φ) = ∼toTr φ
  map_imply' : ∀ φ ψ, toTr (φ ➝ ψ) = toTr φ ➝ toTr ψ
  map_and' : ∀ φ ψ, toTr (φ ⋏ ψ) = toTr φ ⋏ toTr ψ
  map_or'  : ∀ φ ψ, toTr (φ ⋎ ψ) = toTr φ ⋎ toTr ψ

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False

  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

class HomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β] where
  map_top : ∀ (f : F), f ⊤ = ⊤
  map_bot : ∀ (f : F), f ⊥ = ⊥
  map_neg : ∀ (f : F) (φ : α), f (∼ φ) = ∼f φ
  map_imply : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ➝ ψ) = f φ ➝ f ψ
  map_and : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋏ ψ) = f φ ⋏ f ψ
  map_or  : ∀ (f : F) (φ ψ : α), f (φ ⋎ ψ) = f φ ⋎ f ψ

attribute [simp] HomClass.map_top HomClass.map_bot HomClass.map_neg HomClass.map_imply HomClass.map_and HomClass.map_or

namespace HomClass

variable (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [LogicalConnective α] [LogicalConnective β] [FunLike F α β]
variable [HomClass F α β]
variable (f : F) (a b : α)

instance : CoeFun F (fun _ => α → β) := by exact?

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False

  wedge := And

/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

@[reducible]
instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

@[simp] lemma Prop.top_eq : ⊤ = True := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.bot_eq : ⊥ = False := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.neg_eq (φ : Prop) : ∼φ = ¬φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.arrow_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ➝ ψ) = (φ → ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.and_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋏ ψ) = (φ ∧ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.or_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⋎ ψ) = (φ ∨ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma Prop.iff_eq (φ ψ : Prop) : (φ ⭤ ψ) = (φ ↔ ψ) := by simp[LogicalConnective.iff, iff_iff_implies_and_implies]

instance : DeMorgan Prop where
  verum := by simp
  falsum := by simp
  imply := fun _ _ => by simp[imp_iff_not_or]
  and := fun _ _ => by simp[-not_and, not_and_or]
  or := fun _ _ => by simp[not_or]
  neg := fun _ => by simp

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

  Vee.vee

  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥

namespace LogicalConnective

variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

infix:61 " ⭤ " => LogicalConnective.iff

end

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

end

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

  arrow : α → α → α

  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where

  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/--

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

end

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := True
  bot := False
  tilde := Not
  arrow := fun P Q => (P → Q)
  wedge := And
  vee := Or

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

section
variable {α : Type*} [LogicalConnective α]

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

end

instance PropLogicSymbols : LogicalConnective Prop where
  top := by exact?

content_full:
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

namespace LogicalConnective

@[match_pattern] def iff (a b : α) := (a ➝ b) ⋏ (b ➝ a)

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

infixr:69 " ⋏ " => Wedge.wedge

infixr:68 " ⋎ " => Vee.vee

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde
  Arrow.arrow
  Wedge.wedge
  Vee.vee

end logicNotation

class DeMorgan (F : Type*) [LogicalConnective F] where
  verum           : ∼(⊤ : F) = ⊥
  falsum          : ∼(⊥ : F) = ⊤
  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

attribute [simp] DeMorgan.verum DeMorgan.falsum DeMorgan.and DeMorgan.or DeMorgan.neg

/-- Introducing `∼φ` as an abbreviation of `φ ➝ ⊥`. -/
class NegAbbrev (F : Type*) [Tilde F] [Arrow F] [Bot F] where
  neg {φ : F} : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥
-- attribute [simp] NegAbbrev.neg

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

namespace LO

section logicNotation

@[notation_class] class Tilde (α : Type*) where
  tilde : α → α

@[notation_class] class Arrow (α : Type*) where
  arrow : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Wedge (α : Type*) where
  wedge : α → α → α

@[notation_class] class Vee (α : Type*) where
  vee : α → α → α

class LogicalConnective (α : Type*)
  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

prefix:75 "∼" => Tilde.tilde

infixr:60 " ➝ " => Arrow.arrow

attribute [match_pattern]
  Tilde.tilde

  Vee.vee

  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

  extends Top α, Bot α, Tilde α, Arrow α, Wedge α, Vee α

  imply (φ ψ : F) : (φ ➝ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ψ
  and (φ ψ : F)   : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ
  or (φ ψ : F)    : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ
  neg (φ : F)     : ∼∼φ = φ

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Vorspiel

/-!
# Logic Symbols

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.
* `LO.LogicalConnective.Hom` is defined so that `f : F →ˡᶜ G` is a homomorphism from `F` to `G`, i.e.,
a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/

This file defines structure that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$
and their homomorphisms.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.

a function that preserves logical connectives.

/-!

and their homomorphisms.

* `LO.LogicalConnective` is defined so that `LO.LogicalConnective F` is a type that has logical connectives $\top, \bot, \land, \lor, \to, \lnot$.

a function that preserves logical connectives.

-/
